newsitem.title: USA: Commercial Metals investing $70 mln in new mill.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Metals investing $70 mln in new mill.

text.p: Commercial Metals Co said Tuesday it plans to invest $70 million in a new rolling mill project at its SMI Steel South Carolina minimill at Cayce, S.C.
The project will double the annual steel rolling capacity of the facility to 700,000 tons, from 350,000, it said.
To reach the rolling mill's full operating capacity, melt shop production will also have to be increased with a relatively modest capital expenditure in the future, it said.
Stanley Rabin, president and chief executive officer, said the new rolling mill will be similar to the company's mill at its Structural Metals Inc.'s Seguin, Texas plant with some refinements,
He said the new plan will enable Commercial Metals to offer a broader product line including steel reinforcing bars, merchant bar products, structural shapes and special bars.
The new mill will be built adjacent to the existing rolling mill, the company said. Its daily operations will not be affected during the construction period, it said.
Construction will begin this month and the new rolling mill is expected to start up in February 1999, it said.
The project includes a reheat furnace; a state-of- the-art, 17-stand in-line rolling mill; in-line straightening; a cooling bed; and automated bundling and stacking systems.
SMI Steel South Carolina recycles scrap metal by melting it and then shaping it into steel bar products marketed throughout the Southeast and Eastern U.S.
